summary: Section 414 of the Companies Act, 2013 explains how the pay and work rules for Members of the Tribunal and the Appellate Tribunal are decided. It promises that once a person is appointed as a Member, their pay and work conditions cannot be changed to make them worse. This protects the Members from unfair pay cuts after they take the job.
points: The salary and allowances of Members shall be prescribed by the authorities.
The other terms and conditions of service of Members shall also be prescribed.
The salary and allowances of Members cannot be changed to their disadvantage after appointment.
The terms and conditions of service cannot be made worse for Members after they are appointed.
example: Aarav was recently appointed as a Member of the Tribunal for the company Sparkle Logistics Private Limited. When he started, his salary and work benefits were officially set by the prescribed rules. A few months later, the management wanted to reduce his monthly salary and lower his official allowances because the company faced budget issues. However, because of the law protecting his position, his salary and benefits cannot be reduced or made worse after his appointment. Aarav's pay remains safe from any such disadvantageous changes.

terms.meaning: A specialized official body set up to deal with specific legal disputes.
Decided or laid down by the rules made under the law.
A situation that makes things worse or less favorable than before.

watch: People often mistakenly think that a Member's salary can be lowered if the organization faces financial trouble, but the law forbids making their terms worse after appointment.
